title: Reliability Ops Atlas — 90-day cross-functional playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a working playbook (90d horizon) to align platform, serving runtime, console, product, SRE and solutions-engineering on a coherent SLO program and operational cadence for model-serving products. The aim is to:
- Establish measurable service-level objectives for core inference surfaces (text-generation API, embeddings, KV-cache-backed chat).
- Deliver telemetry and alerting primitives so feature teams can own SLOs with minimum ops friction.
- Define cross-functional rollout steps, runbooks and experiment gates for canary/A-B migrations and fallback policies.

Key constraints/assumptions (read before planning):
- We must maintain API availability during regional infra maintenance windows (no >5m customer-impacting outages expected).
- Serving runtime provides variants: fast-32 (low-latency), high-thru (batched), quantized-16. Not all variants are functionally identical — fallback behavior must be explicit.
- We have limited tagging of requests today; telemetry work is required to get token-level cost and model variant attribution.

Top-level goals (90d):
1) Baseline & publicize SLOs for the hosted API (generation + embeddings) — P95 latency and availability targets and error-rate SLOs.
2) Ship telemetry pipeline enhancements so teams can slice SLOs by model family, region, customer tier.
3) Create a simple SLO onboarding template + automation so 8 target product owners can onboard by end of quarter.
4) Validate rollback/fallback flows with 3+ canary runs and at least one cross-region failover drill.

Stakeholders and primary owners:
- Program lead / facilitator: Aisha Patel (platform-engineering) — accountable for cross-team coordination, milestones.
- SLO design & instrumentation: Diego Morales (observability) — responsible for metric schema, dashboards.
- Runtime & fallback policies: Samir Kapoor (serving-runtime) — owns model variant compatibility matrix and fallback orchestration.
- Console/UX integration: Elena Rossi (product-console) — shipping SLO dashboard templates and onboarding UX.
- SRE liaison: Ruth Li (site-reliability-engineering) — owns oncall drills, runbooks and escalation matrix.

Success metrics (what good looks like):
- Public SLO doc published and accessible from Console (per-route) by D+45.
- Instrumentation: 95% of production routes emit required SLO metrics with model_variant tag by D+60.
- Onboarding: 6 teams (Generation, Embeddings, Re-ranking, Chat, Dedup, Metrics) onboarded to SLO templates with alerted runbooks by D+85.
- Operational readiness: one full failover drill to secondary region with automated rollback validated by SRE by D+90.
- Measurable customer impact: reduce P99 latency tail for production traffic by 10% for targeted routes where batching/quantization recommendations applied.

90-day timeline (milestones and high level tasks):
- Week 0–2 (Discovery + baseline)
  - Rapid audit of current K8s/infra telemetry: what metrics, tags, and traces exist today. (Diego)
  - Inventory of active routes, model variants, and owner contacts. (Aisha + Runtime team)
  - Host quick cross-team kickoff and confirm cadence (weekly sync + triage wedge).
- Week 3–6 (Instrumentation & SLO schema)
  - Define minimal SLO metric schema: availability (4xx/5xx), latency histograms (per-request tokenized), error-type tagging, traffic-weight. (Diego)
  - Implement producer changes in runtime to add model_variant and region tags. (Samir)
  - Prototype per-route SLO dashboard in Console. (Elena)
- Week 7–10 (Templates & automation)
  - Ship SLO onboarding template (SLO target, burn-rate thresholds, runbook link). (Aisha + Elena)
  - Add automation to register SLOs in observability stack (one-click for product owners). (Diego)
  - Start onboarding pilot product teams (Generation + Embeddings).
- Week 11–13 (Canaries, fallback tests)
  - Run scheduled canary deployments for quantized/fast variants on low-risk customers. Validate rollback. (Samir + SRE)
  - Run a cross-region failover tabletop then a live drill (window scheduled with infra). (Ruth)
- Week 14 (Closeout + retrospective)
  - Capture learnings, update playbook, determine next 90d slate (expansion to Dedicated/Private).

Operational details (practical runbook items):
- SLO definitions (initial suggested targets):
  - Generation API availability SLO: 99.95% (rolling 30d) — measured as successful response rate for synchronous generation calls.
  - Generation latency SLO: P95 < 1800ms for small models (<=2k tokens), P95 < 3500ms for large models (>2k tokens).
  - Embeddings SLO: P95 < 800ms, availability 99.99% (higher bar given embedding customers are latency-sensitive).
  - Error SLO (per-route): client-visible errors (4xx) baseline, server errors (5xx) < 0.05% rolling 7d.
- Alerts / burn rate thresholds:
  - Burn rate alert 1: 2x expected error budget consumption over 1h -> passive notify (Slack #slo-alerts + ticket auto-created).
  - Burn rate alert 2: 5x over 15m -> page SRE oncall + product owner.
  - Latency tail alert: P99 > 2x SLO for 30m -> runbook run.
- Immediate runbook actions (triage steps):
  1) Gather telemetry (last 30m traces, top 10 slow traces, model_variant distribution).
  2) Check runtime pool utilization and GPU backpressure metrics.
  3) If degraded, switch route to fallback variant (policy: prefer fast-32 then quantized-16 then high-thru).
  4) If fallback fails or increases errors: escalate to SRE, enable global rate limiter to shed non-critical traffic.
  5) Postmortem: short RCA within 72h, link to SLO incident page.

Cross-team dependencies and asks (what I need from you):
- Observability: Diego — finalize metric schema and confirm storage cost impact (esp. token-level histograms).
- Runtime: Samir — implement tags + ensure fallback path is automated and has circuit-breaker.
- Console: Elena — ship per-route SLO view, permissioned to team owners.
- Product: PMs — agree on per-route SLO targets and customer tier differentiation.
- SRE: Ruth — runbook review, drill schedule and oncall paging configuration.

Open questions / discussion points (to resolve in week 1–3):
- Which routes are considered "critical" vs "non-critical" for rate limiting? Need product input.
- Do we allow model-variant fallbacks to change model semantics? (acceptable for embeddings; less so for compositional generation).
- Token-level histogram retention policy — 7d raw, aggregated 90d? Need cost estimate.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Instrumentation rollout causes extra latency or cardinality explosion.
  - Mitigation: start with sampling (1–5%) for token histograms, ramp to 100% after profiling.
- Risk: Fallback variants produce unacceptable quality regressions.
  - Mitigation: define quality gates (prompt-eval harness) and expose a QA toggle per-customer.
- Risk: Teams overloaded with onboarding work.
  - Mitigation: provide template + automated registration flow, offer two SE office hours/week for onboarding.

Communication cadence and channels:
- Weekly sync (60m) — program status, blockers, open actions (Aisha to run).
- Triage wedge (30m, MWF) for active incidents during rollout.
- Slack channels: #reliability-atlas (updates), #slo-alerts (automated alerts).
- Confluence page for canonical docs (link above).

Immediate next actions (this week):
- [Aisha] Finalize kickoff invite and weekly calendar.
- [Diego] Post metric schema draft in the doc and estimate Prometheus/TSDB cost.
- [Samir] Prototype model_variant tagging in dev cluster and share perf numbers.
- [Elena] Wireframe the Console SLO card and share for feedback.
- [Ruth] Draft runbook template and paging matrix for SLO burns.

Notes-to-self / scratch ideas:
- Could be useful to ship a "SLO status" badge in Console so internal teams can surface to customers.
- Consider bundling a lightweight SLO QA checklist into onboarding so SEs know what tests to run.
- Long-term: integrate Optimize recommendations with SLO dashboard (suggest quantization/batching to meet SLOs at lower cost).

Appendix: quick contact list
- Program lead: Aisha Patel — aisha@redwood.ai
- Observability (SLO metrics): Diego Morales — diego@redwood.ai
- Runtime & fallbacks: Samir Kapoor — samir@redwood.ai
- Console / UX: Elena Rossi — elena@redwood.ai
- SRE lead: Ruth Li — ruth@redwood.ai

Unresolved decisions (capture for the first retro):
- Acceptable quality delta thresholds for fallback by route (TBD).
- Final retention windows for token histograms vs aggregated percentiles.
- SLA language vs SLO (legal review needed before publishing external-facing guarantees).
